at æde.explanation: "At æde" means "to eat" for animals: Løven æder kød (The lion eats meat). For people, use at spise (to eat): Jeg spiser frokost (I eat lunch). Said about a person, æde sounds rough.

sentence.da: Hunden vil gerne **æde** kødet nu.
sentence.en: The dog would like to eat the meat now.

at ændre.explanation: "At ændre" means "to change" or "to alter", to make something different: Jeg ændrer planen (I am changing the plan). To swap one thing for another, use at skifte: Jeg skifter dæk (I change tires).

sentence.da: Vi må **ændre** planen, fordi det regner.
sentence.en: We have to change the plan because it is raining.

at ændre på.explanation: "At ændre på" means "to change something", to make part of it different: Vi ændrer på planen (We are changing the plan). To become different by itself, use at ændre sig (to change): Vejret ændrer sig (The weather is changing).

sentence.da: Vi kan **ændre på** planen i morgen.
sentence.en: We can change the plan tomorrow.

at ændre sig.explanation: "At ændre sig" means "to change" by itself: Byen ændrer sig hurtigt (The city changes fast). To change something, drop sig: Jeg ændrer planen (I change the plan).

sentence.da: Vejret vil **ændre sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: The weather will change tomorrow.

at ærgre sig.explanation: "At ærgre sig" means "to be annoyed" about something that went wrong, with a bit of disappointment: Jeg ærgrer mig over, at jeg kom for sent (I am annoyed that I was late). For someone else, use sig: Hun ærgrer sig (She is annoyed).

sentence.da: Hun vil **ærgre sig**, hvis hun glemmer billetten.
sentence.en: She will be annoyed if she forgets the ticket.

en æbleskive.explanation: "En æbleskive" means "an æbleskive", a round, puffy Danish pancake. The name means "apple slice" (æble = apple, skive = slice).

sentence.da: Vi spiser en varm **æbleskive** med sukker og syltetøj.
sentence.en: We eat a warm æbleskive with sugar and jam.

en ægtemand.explanation: "En ægtemand" means "a husband", a man in a marriage: Hun præsenterede sin ægtemand for os (She introduced her husband to us). In everyday speech, Danes often just say min mand (my husband).

sentence.da: Min **ægtemand** laver mad i aften.
sentence.en: My husband is cooking tonight.

en ændring.explanation: "En ændring" means "a change", when something becomes different: Vi har lavet en ændring i menuen (We made a change on the menu). To swap one thing for another, say at skifte (to switch): at skifte sko (to change shoes).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **ændring** i planen.
sentence.en: There is a big change in the plan.

en æske.explanation: "En æske" means "a box", usually a smaller one made of cardboard: en æske chokolade (a box of chocolates). A big box for packing is en kasse (a crate / large box).

sentence.da: Hun giver mig en **æske** chokolade.
sentence.en: She gives me a box of chocolates.

et æble.explanation: "Et æble" means "an apple". The letter æ sounds like the e in bed, but longer. Danish joins words together: æblekage (apple cake) is æble plus kage (cake), and æblejuice (apple juice) works the same way.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser et rødt **æble**.
sentence.en: I eat a red apple.

et æg.explanation: "Et æg" means "an egg". The letter æ sounds like the e in bed. Two common kinds are kogt æg (boiled egg) and spejlæg (fried egg).

sentence.da: Jeg koger et **æg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I boil an egg for breakfast.

et æggebæger.explanation: "Et æggebæger" means "an egg cup", the little cup that holds a boiled egg upright: Jeg sætter ægget i æggebægeret (I put the egg in the egg cup).

sentence.da: Han sætter det kogte æg i et **æggebæger**.
sentence.en: He puts the boiled egg in an egg cup.

et ægtepar.explanation: "Et ægtepar" means "a married couple": De er et ægtepar (They are a married couple). For two people who are together but not married, use et kærestepar (a couple).

sentence.da: Det gamle **ægtepar** går tur hver dag.
sentence.en: The old married couple takes a walk every day.

et ægteskab.explanation: "Et ægteskab" means "a marriage", the life of two people who are married: Deres ægteskab er meget lykkeligt (Their marriage is very happy). The wedding itself is et bryllup (a wedding).

sentence.da: Deres **ægteskab** har holdt i tyve år.
sentence.en: Their marriage has lasted twenty years.

et ærme.explanation: "Et ærme" means "a sleeve", the part of a shirt or jacket that covers your arm: Skjorten har lange ærmer (The shirt has long sleeves).

sentence.da: Der er et hul i mit venstre **ærme**.
sentence.en: There is a hole in my left sleeve.

ægte.explanation: "Ægte" means "genuine" or "real": ægte læder (genuine leather). It also fits people and feelings: en ægte ven (a true friend).

sentence.da: Er den her taske af **ægte** læder?
sentence.en: Is this bag made of genuine leather?

ældre.explanation: "Ældre" means "older" or "elderly". It is the step up from gammel (old), as in ældre end mig (older than me). De ældre is a polite way to say elderly people.

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældre** end mig.
sentence.en: My brother is older than me.

ældst.explanation: "Ældst" means "oldest" and is the step up from ældre (older): Han er ældst (He is the oldest).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældst** af os.
sentence.en: My brother is the oldest of us.

ærgerlig.explanation: "Ærgerlig" means "unfortunate" or "a shame", for a situation that goes wrong: Det er ærgerligt, at du ikke kan komme (It is a shame you cannot come).

sentence.da: Det var en **ærgerlig** misforståelse.
sentence.en: That was an unfortunate misunderstanding.

ærlig.explanation: "Ærlig" means "honest", saying what is true: Vær ærlig! (Be honest!). Ærligt talt (honestly) often starts a frank remark: Ærligt talt, jeg kan ikke lide det (Honestly, I do not like it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne være **ærlig** over for dig.
sentence.en: I would like to be honest with you.

ærlighed.explanation: "Ærlighed" means "honesty", telling the truth and not cheating: Ærlighed varer længst (Honesty lasts longest). Han er kendt for sin ærlighed (He is known for his honesty).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter pris på **ærlighed** hos mine venner.
sentence.en: I appreciate honesty in my friends.

ærter.explanation: "Ærter" means "peas". Example: Jeg kan godt lide ærter (I like peas). For peas in a dish, say grønne ærter (green peas).

sentence.da: Suppen har grønne **ærter**.
sentence.en: The soup has green peas.
